Head.title: Head & Neuro Radiology Reference
Head.content:
Authoritative neuroimaging reference across Non-Contrast CT (ASPECTS scoring, acute hemorrhage, trauma), CT Angiography (Circle of Willis, carotids, aneurysm, dissection), high-resolution Skull Radiography (Townes, Waters, Caldwell views), and volumetric MRI protocols.

ASPECTS Stroke Scoring & CT Windowing

The Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) is a 10-point quantitative topographic CT assessment for MCA acute ischemic stroke. Windowing for acute ischemia requires narrow brain window (W: 30–40, L: 30–35) to accentuate subtle gray-white junction dedifferentiation.

Circle of Willis & TOF-MRA Physics

Flow-related enhancement exploits unsaturated, fully magnetized spins entering the 3D imaging slab. Complete vascular assessment must include the anterior communicating (ACom), bilateral A1/A2, posterior communicating (PCom), basilar bifurcation, and bilateral MCA M1/M2 branches.

procedures.name: Non-Contrast Head CT (Acute Stroke / Trauma / ICH)
indications: Acute ischemic stroke triage within 4.5h window (ASPECTS score)
Traumatic brain injury (epidural, subdural, subarachnoid hemorrhage)
Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and intraventricular extension
Elevated intracranial pressure, midline shift, and brain herniation

technique.Slice / Interval: 0.625 mm raw acquisition, reformatted at 4.0 mm contiguous

procedures.positioning: Patient supine, head immobilized in dedicated head holder. Chin tucked so baseline (orbitomeatal line) is parallel to gantry plane to minimize eye lens radiation.
procedures.notes: Hyperdense MCA sign indicates acute thromboembolism. Look for loss of insular ribbon, lentiform obscuration, and sulcal effacement.

procedures.name: CT Angiography (CTA) Head & Neck
indications: Acute stroke large vessel occlusion (LVO) detection for endovascular thrombectomy
Carotid and vertebral artery dissection (intimal flap, intramural hematoma)
Arteriovenous malformations (AVM) and dural AV fistulas
Internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis quantification (NASCET criteria)
procedures.contrast: 60–80 mL non-ionic iodinated contrast (350–370 mg I/mL) @ 4.5–5.0 mL/s + 40 mL saline flush

technique.Triggering: Bolus tracking on aortic arch (100 HU trigger threshold) or automated smart prep
technique.Scan Coverage: Aortic arch through Circle of Willis to vertex
technique.Reconstructions: 0.625 mm axial, coronal/sagittal MIP (15–20 mm slab), 3D VR

procedures.positioning: Patient supine, head straight in head holder, shoulders pulled down slightly. Arms resting comfortably at sides.
procedures.notes: Multiphasic CTA (arterial, peak venous, late venous) provides robust collateral flow grading in acute ischemic stroke.

procedures.name: Skull Radiography (AP, Lateral, Towne's View)
indications: Calvarial fracture evaluation, linear and depressed skull fractures
Paget disease of bone (cotton wool appearance)
Post-operative craniotomy flap and burr hole alignment
Foreign body localization and gunshot projectile assessment

technique.Focal Spot: Small focal spot (0.6 mm) for high spatial bone detail
technique.Projections: AP Axial (Towne's 30° caudad to OML), Lateral (CR 5cm above EAM)

procedures.positioning: Towne's view: Patient supine or erect, chin tucked to align orbitomeatal line (OML) perpendicular to IR. Angle CR 30° caudad through foramen magnum. Lateral: Head in true lateral, inter-pupillary line perpendicular to IR.
procedures.notes: Towne's view projects the dorsum sellae and posterior clinoid processes within the shadow of the foramen magnum.

procedures.name: Paranasal Sinuses & Facial Bones (Water's & Caldwell)
indications: Orbital blowout fracture with maxillary sinus herniation
Nasal bone fracture with septal deviation

technique.Projections: Parietoacanthial (Water's view), PA Axial (Caldwell view 15° caudad)

procedures.positioning: Erect posture MANDATORY to demonstrate horizontal air-fluid levels. Water's: Chin resting on bucky, nose 1 cm away, orbitomeatal line at 37° to IR plane. Central ray exits at acanthion.
procedures.notes: Always inspect the orbital floor and teardrop soft-tissue density hanging into the maxillary antrum in blowout fractures.

Neck.title: Cervical Spine & Neck Radiology Reference
Neck.content:
Multimodality diagnostic protocols for cervical soft tissues, airway patency, cervical adenopathy, thyroid nodules, carotid bifurcation stenosis, and cervical spine osteoligamentous integrity.

Carotid Stenosis Criteria (NASCET)

Calculated as: % Stenosis = (1 - [narrowest lumen / normal distal ICA lumen]) x 100%. Severe stenosis (≥70%) carries critical thromboembolic stroke risk and benefits from carotid endarterectomy or stenting.

procedures.name: Contrast-Enhanced Soft Tissue Neck CT
indications: Deep neck space infection (retropharyngeal, peritonsillar, Ludwig angina)
Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (staging of primary and nodal metastases)
Thyroid mass, substernal goiter, and parathyroid adenoma localization
Vocal cord paralysis, laryngeal trauma, and pyriform sinus lesions
Branchial cleft cyst, thyroglossal duct cyst, and salivary gland tumors
procedures.contrast: 75–100 mL non-ionic iodinated contrast (300–350 mg I/mL) @ 2.5–3.0 mL/s, scan delay 65–70 seconds

technique.Slice: 0.625 mm acquisition, reconstructed 2.0 mm contiguous axial, coronal, sagittal
technique.Coverage: Skull base to aortic arch (carotid bifurcation to mediastinum)

procedures.positioning: Patient supine, head extended slightly. Instruct patient to swallow saliva BEFORE scan start, then maintain quiet breathing with ZERO swallowing during beam sweep.
procedures.notes: Valsalva maneuver or phonating 'eeeee' may be added for dedicated piriform sinus and vocal cord mucosal distension.

procedures.name: Cervical Spine Radiography (AP, Lateral, Open-Mouth Odontoid)
indications: Trauma cervical spine clearance (Canadian C-Spine / NEXUS criteria)
Cervical spondylosis, neural foraminal stenosis, and disc height loss
Odontoid fracture (Type I, II, III) and atlantoaxial subluxation
Rheumatoid arthritis C1-C2 pannus and retro-odontoid instability

technique.kVp / mAs: Lateral: 75–80 kVp, 20–32 mAs; AP: 70–75 kVp, 10–14 mAs; Open-mouth: 70 kVp, 8–12 mAs
technique.SID: 180 cm (72 inches) for lateral to reduce magnification; 100 cm for AP/Odontoid
technique.Landmarks: C1 to C7-T1 junction must be completely visible

procedures.positioning: Lateral: Patient erect, shoulders depressed (weights in hands if needed to expose C7-T1). Open-mouth: Mouth wide open, line from lower edge of upper incisors to mastoid tip perpendicular to IR, patient phonating 'ah' to depress tongue.
procedures.notes: Verify the 4 parallel lines on lateral: anterior vertebral line, posterior vertebral line, spinolaminar line, and spinous process line.

procedures.name: Soft Tissue Lateral Neck (Airway & Retropharyngeal Space)
indications: Retropharyngeal abscess (pathological widening of prevertebral soft tissue)
Foreign body ingestion (fish bone, coin, battery) in hypopharynx/cervical esophagus

technique.kVp / mAs: 65–70 kVp (lower kVp enhances soft tissue contrast), 8–12 mAs
technique.Exposure: During deep inspiration with neck slightly extended

procedures.positioning: Patient standing or seated in true lateral. Arms behind back to prevent shoulder superimposition over lower neck and thoracic inlet.
procedures.notes: Normal retropharyngeal width: C2-C3 < 7 mm (or < 1/3 vertebral width); C6-C7 < 14 mm in children, < 22 mm in adults.

Chest.title: Thorax & Cardiovascular Radiology Reference
Chest.content:
Exhaustive thoracic imaging protocols covering Chest Radiography (PA, Lateral, Lordotic), High-Resolution CT (HRCT) for interstitial lung diseases, CT Pulmonary Angiography (CTPA) for pulmonary embolism, Aortic dissection CTA, and Cardiac MRI.

PE Triage & CTPA Injection Dynamics

Pulmonary arterial opacification requires high flow rates (≥4.0 mL/s) with bolus tracking ROI placed on the main pulmonary artery trunk. Threshold trigger set to 100 HU with automated shallow inspiration breathing to avoid the transient interruption of contrast (TIC) effect from IVC unopacified blood rush.

procedures.name: High-Resolution CT (HRCT) Chest
indications: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF / UIP pattern: honeycombing, traction bronchiectasis)
Non-Specific Interstitial Pneumonia (NSIP: subpleural ground-glass opacities)
Bronchiectasis, small airway bronchiolitis, and air trapping (mosaic attenuation)
procedures.contrast: None (non-contrast ensures pristine assessment of lung parenchyma)

technique.Slice Thickness: 0.625–1.0 mm reconstructed with sharp high-spatial frequency lung kernel
technique.Spacing: Contiguous volumetric helical acquisition or 10 mm spaced axial HRCT
technique.Expiratory Phase: Add 3–5 low-dose expiratory slices to confirm air trapping
technique.Prone Scans: Prone positioning if needed to clear dependent atelectasis

procedures.positioning: Patient supine, arms fully elevated above head. Suspended end-inspiration on second full breath-hold.
procedures.notes: Honeycombing is defined as clustered subpleural cystic spaces (3–10 mm) with shared thick walls in multiple layers.

procedures.name: CT Pulmonary Angiography (CTPA - Pulmonary Embolism)
indications: Acute pulmonary embolism (PE) rule-out with elevated D-dimer or high Wells score
Saddle embolus causing acute right ventricular strain
Pulmonary artery aneurysm or arteriovenous fistula (PAVM)
procedures.contrast: 60–75 mL high-concentration iodinated contrast (350–370 mg I/mL) @ 4.0–5.0 mL/s via 18G/20G antecubital IV + 40 mL saline chaser

technique.kVp / mAs: 100 kVp (increases iodine k-edge photoelectric absorption) / auto mAs
technique.Bolus Tracking: ROI on main pulmonary artery trunk, trigger threshold 100–120 HU
technique.Scan Direction: Caudocranial (feet-to-head) to minimize respiratory motion at diaphragmatic bases

procedures.positioning: Supine, arms overhead. Instruction: 'Take a gentle breath in and hold your breath'. Avoid deep Valsalva which causes transient dilution of contrast.
procedures.notes: Assess right ventricle to left ventricle (RV/LV) diameter ratio in axial view: RV/LV > 1.0 indicates significant RV strain/submassive PE.

procedures.name: CTA Thoracic Aorta (Dissection / Aneurysm Protocol)
indications: Acute aortic syndrome: Stanford Type A vs Type B aortic dissection
Intramural hematoma (IMH) and penetrating atherosclerotic ulcer (PAU)
Thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) sizing and pre-TEVAR planning
Traumatic aortic pseudoaneurysm / isthmus transection in deceleration trauma
procedures.contrast: 80–100 mL contrast @ 4.0–4.5 mL/s + 40 mL saline flush

technique.ECG Gating: Prospective or retrospective ECG gating to eliminate ascending aortic root pulsation artifact
technique.Scan Range: Lung apices through iliac bifurcation (entire aorta)
technique.Phases: Unenhanced scan (to detect high-attenuation crescent of IMH) followed by arterial CTA

procedures.positioning: Patient supine, arms raised. Fast gantry rotation (0.28s) synchronized with ECG R-wave trigger.
procedures.notes: Type A involves the ascending aorta and requires emergent surgical repair; Type B is distal to left subclavian origin.

procedures.name: Chest Radiography (Standard PA & Lateral)
indications: Pneumothorax (visceral pleural line with absent peripheral lung markings)
Pleural effusion (blunting of costophrenic and cardiophrenic angles)
Congestive heart failure (cardiomegaly, Kerley B lines, cephalization of vessels)
Pulmonary nodules, masses, and mediastinal widening

technique.kVp / mAs: PA: 110–125 kVp (high kVp technique penetrates mediastinum), 3–5 mAs; Lateral: 120 kVp, 8–15 mAs
technique.SID: 180 cm (72 inches) to minimize cardiac magnification
technique.Focal Spot: Large focal spot (1.2 mm) with high mA for short exposure time (<10 ms)
technique.Breathing: Suspended full inspiration on second breath (count 10 posterior ribs above diaphragm)

procedures.positioning: PA: Patient standing facing bucky, chin elevated on rest, hands on hips with elbows rolled forward to rotate scapulae laterally out of lung fields. Lateral: Left side against bucky (reduces heart magnification), arms raised overhead holding support bar.
procedures.notes: Cardiothoracic ratio (CTR) on PA view should be <= 50% in healthy adults. Lateral view confirms retrosternal and retrocardiac clear spaces.

procedures.name: Portable / Supine AP Chest Radiography (ICU Protocol)
indications: Endotracheal tube (ETT) tip verification (ideal: 3–5 cm above carina at T2-T4 level)
Central venous catheter (CVC) tip position (ideal: cavoatrial junction)
Enteric nasogastric (NGT) tube tip localization (below diaphragm in stomach)
Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) monitoring and barotrauma/pneumothorax

technique.Grid: Virtual grid software or anti-scatter mobile grid

procedures.positioning: Detector behind patient's back. Elevate head of bed as much as tolerated. Tube angled perpendicular to sternum.
procedures.notes: Remember: Heart appears 15–20% magnified on AP portable radiographs compared to standard PA.

procedures.name: Cardiac MRI protocols, Planning and Techniques
indications: The right atrioventricular valve/tricuspid valve separates the right atrium and right ventricle
The left atrioventricular valve/mitral valve separates the left atrium and left ventricle
The right semilunar/pulmonary valve lies between the right ventricle and pulmonary trunk
The left semilunar/aortic valve lies between the left ventricle and the aorta
Fibrous pericardium is the outer layer which attaches to the diaphragm, vena cava, aorta and sternum
Parietal pericardium is the middle serous layer

procedures.notes: For the assessment of aorta and great vessels diseases

indications: Instruct the patient to breathe in, but not too deeply.
Instruct the patient to breathe out and then to stop breathing.
Ask the patient to breathe normally after the scan (usually for under 20 minutes).

Abdomen.title: Abdomen & Gastrointestinal Radiology Reference
Abdomen.content:
Complete diagnostic protocols for acute abdominal pain, parenchymal liver lesions (HCC, hemangioma, metastases), pancreatic adenocarcinoma, renal calculi, urinary tract urothelial staging, and plain film bowel obstruction assessment.

Multiphase Liver CT Hemodynamics

Liver has dual blood supply: 75% portal vein, 25% hepatic artery. Normal parenchyma enhances on portal venous phase (70s). Hypervascular tumors (HCC, FNH) receive exclusive arterial supply, producing intense arterial enhancement (30–35s) followed by wash-out on portal venous/delayed phases.

procedures.name: Triple-Phase / Multiphase Liver CT (HCC Protocol)
indications: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) screening in cirrhosis (LI-RADS classification)
Focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) with central scar vs hepatic adenoma
Cavernous hemangioma (peripheral nodular puddling with centripetal fill-in)
Colorectal cancer liver metastases (hypervascular vs hypovascular staging)
Pre-operative hepatic resection and liver transplant volumetry
procedures.contrast: 120–150 mL non-ionic contrast (350 mg I/mL) @ 4.0–5.0 mL/s via large bore IV + 40 mL saline

technique.Phase 1 - Non-contrast: Baseline detection of calcifications, fat, and glycogen stores
technique.Slice / Window: 1.0 mm raw, 2.5 mm reformats; Liver Window: WW: 150, WL: 70 HU

procedures.positioning: Patient supine, arms elevated above head. Scan performed on suspended full inspiration.
procedures.notes: LI-RADS 5 criteria: Non-rim arterial phase hyperenhancement + washout appearance + enhancing capsule or size >= 10 mm with growth.

procedures.name: CT Abdomen & Pelvis with IV Contrast (Acute Abdomen)
indications: Acute appendicitis (dilated appendix >6 mm, wall thickening, periappendiceal fat stranding, appendicolith)
Acute diverticulitis (sigmoid colonic wall thickening, pericolic fat haziness, abscess)
Small bowel obstruction (transition point, closed-loop strangulation, mesenteric swirl)
Bowel ischemia and pneumatosis intestinalis with portal venous gas
procedures.contrast: 100–120 mL IV contrast @ 3.0 mL/s, scanned at portal venous phase (70–75s). Oral/rectal contrast per institutional protocol.

technique.kVp / mAs: 120 kVp, auto mA modulation (CARE Dose / ASiR)
technique.Slice: 0.625 mm raw acquisition, 2.5 mm axial, coronal, and sagittal MPR

procedures.positioning: Patient supine, arms comfortably overhead. Single breath-hold (10–12 seconds).
procedures.notes: Coronal multiplanar reformats are essential for tracing mesenteric vessels and identifying internal hernia orifices.

procedures.name: CT Urography (Split-Bolus Hematuria Protocol)
indications: Painless gross hematuria or high-risk microscopic hematuria
Upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) of renal pelvis and ureters
Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) staging and vascular invasion (renal vein / IVC thrombus)
Ureteral stricture, obstruction, and retroperitoneal fibrosis
procedures.contrast: Split-bolus technique: Bolus 1 (30–40 mL @ 2.0 mL/s) -> 8 min wait -> Bolus 2 (80 mL @ 3.0 mL/s) -> scan at 90s after 2nd bolus. Combines nephrographic + excretory phases in a SINGLE scan!

technique.Reconstruction: 0.625 mm contiguous slices, coronal/sagittal MIP and 3D volume rendering of urinary tract
technique.Hydration: Oral water hydration (500–750 mL) 20 min prior to distend pelvicalyceal system

procedures.positioning: Supine. Full scan from diaphragm through urethra.
procedures.notes: Split bolus dramatically halves patient radiation dose compared to traditional separate 4-phase CT urography.

procedures.name: Abdominal Radiography (KUB - Supine)
indications: Radio-opaque renal and ureteric calculi (calcium oxalate, struvite, cystine stones)
Bowel gas distribution, adynamic ileus, and toxic megacolon
Foreign body ingestion and medical device positioning (ureteric stent, feeding tube)
Abdominal calcifications (porcelain gallbladder, vascular calcifications, nephrocalcinosis)

technique.kVp / mAs: 75–80 kVp (low-medium kVp preserves contrast for calcifications), 25–40 mAs
technique.Breathing: Exposure at end of full expiration (raises diaphragm to optimize coverage)

procedures.positioning: Patient supine, midsagittal plane aligned to midline of table. CR directed perpendicular to iliac crests (L4-L5 level). Lower border must include pubic symphysis to avoid missing distal ureteric calculi.
procedures.notes: Kidneys, Ureters, and Bladder (KUB) outline should be inspected along psoas muscle shadows.

procedures.name: Erect Abdomen / Left Lateral Decubitus (Free Air / Obstruction)
indications: Pneumoperitoneum: Subdiaphragmatic free crescentic gas in bowel perforation
Mechanical small bowel obstruction: multiple central air-fluid levels ('step-ladder' sign)
Large bowel obstruction: peripheral colonic distension with competent ileocecal valve
Volvulus: Sigmoid volvulus ('coffee bean' sign arising from pelvis) vs cecal volvulus

technique.Erect Time: Patient must remain upright or in left lateral decubitus for at least 5–10 MINUTES before exposure to allow free gas to ascend!

procedures.positioning: Erect: Patient stands with back against vertical bucky, CR horizontal 5 cm above iliac crest to capture diaphragms. Decubitus: Patient on left side (liver down, air rises along right flank away from stomach gas bubble).
procedures.notes: As little as 1 mL of free intraperitoneal gas can be detected under the right hemidiaphragm on a well-positioned erect film.

procedures.name: Liver MRI

technique.Sequences: Axial/Coronal T1, T2 TSE, STIR / FS

procedures.positioning: To localize and plan the sequences, it is essential to acquire a three-plane T2 HASTE localizer initially. These fast single-shot localizers have an acquisition time of under 25 seconds and are highly effective in accurately localizing abdominal structures.
procedures.notes: MRI is one of the most useful and rapidly developing diagnostic tools for evaluating liver pathologies. MRI allows the acquisition of images with excellent tissue contrast and anatomical detail. It is particularly effective in visualizing liver tissue and can detect and characterize focal liver lesi

procedures.name: MRCP Planning

technique.Sequences: Axial/Coronal T1, T2 TSE, STIR / FS

procedures.notes: The anatomy of the biliary system is of utmost importance in radiology as it plays a crucial role in the diagnosis and treatment of biliary disorders. Spine.title: Spine & Neuro-Axis Radiology Reference
Spine.content:
Imaging protocols for acute spinal cord trauma, spinal canal stenosis, disc herniation, spondylolisthesis, vertebral compression fractures, and spinal cord tumors.

Denis Three-Column Spine Concept

Anterior Column (ALL, anterior 2/3 vertebral body/disc), Middle Column (posterior 1/3 vertebral body, PLL), Posterior Column (pedicles, facets, lamina, spinous processes). Disruption of 2 or more columns indicates mechanical spinal instability requiring surgical stabilization.

procedures.name: CT Cervical / Thoracic / Lumbar Spine (Bone Trauma)
indications: Traumatic burst fractures and retropulsed bone fragments into spinal canal
Chance fracture (flexion-distraction injury across all 3 columns)
Spondylolysis (pars interarticularis defect) and spondylolisthesis grading
Pathologic compression fractures (osteoporosis vs neoplastic infiltration)
Post-operative pedicle screw placement and fusion cage assessment
procedures.contrast: Usually non-contrast for bone evaluation (IV contrast added if epidural hematoma/abscess suspected)

technique.kVp / mAs: 120–140 kVp (140 kVp for dense shoulders/pelvis), 300–400 mAs
technique.Reconstructions: 0.625 mm contiguous slices, multiplanar coronal and sagittal reformations

procedures.positioning: Patient supine, arms on chest or overhead (for thoracolumbar). Shoulders pulled down for cervical spine.
procedures.notes: Measure percentage spinal canal narrowing caused by retropulsed bone fragments; assess sagittal spinal curvature and facet apposition.

procedures.positioning: AP: Supine with knees and hips flexed to flatten lumbar lordosis and open intervertebral disc spaces. Lateral: True lateral recumbent, CR perpendicular to iliac crest (L4) or 4 cm above crest. L5-S1 Spot: CR angled 5–8° caudad (males) or 8–12° caudad (females) to parallel interspace.
procedures.notes: On 45° obliques, identify the 'Scottie Dog': Eye = pedicle, Ear = superior articular process, Nose = transverse process, Foreleg = inferior articular process, Neck = pars interarticularis.

UpperLimb.title: Upper Extremity MSK & Angiography Reference
UpperLimb.content:
High-resolution orthopedic and vascular imaging of the shoulder girdle, humerus, elbow joint, wrist carpals (scaphoid series), hand, and upper extremity run-off angiography.

Scaphoid Fracture Radiographic Protocols

Scaphoid fractures represent 70% of carpal fractures. Blood supply enters retrograde via the dorsal ridge near the distal pole. Waist and proximal pole fractures carry high risk of avascular necrosis (AVN) and nonunion, mandating a 4-view scaphoid radiographic series with 20° ulnar deviation.

procedures.name: CT Upper Extremity & Joint with 3D Volume Rendering
indications: Complex proximal humerus 3-part and 4-part Neer fractures
Glenoid bone loss measurement (inverted pear appearance, Best-Fit circle method)
Distal radius intra-articular step-off and comminution (Fernandez / Frykman)
Occult scaphoid fracture and nonunion avascular necrosis staging
procedures.contrast: None (unenhanced bone algorithm), or CT Arthrography (intra-articular iodinated contrast for labral/TFCC tears)

technique.Post-processing: Multiplanar reconstructions (MPR) aligned to joint axes, 3D volume rendering with digital subtraction of superimposed bones

procedures.positioning: Shoulder: Patient supine, arm at side in neutral rotation. Wrist: Patient prone in 'Superman' position (arm extended overhead) to place wrist in scanner isocenter and minimize cone-beam artifacts.
procedures.notes: Sub-millimeter volumetric CT accurately detects articular incongruity >= 1.0 mm, which guides surgical fixation.

procedures.name: Shoulder Series (AP Grashey True AP, Scapular Y, Axillary)
indications: Shoulder dislocation: Anterior (95% - subcoracoid) vs Posterior (5% - lightbulb sign on AP)
Hill-Sachs lesion (posterolateral humeral head impaction) and Bankart fracture
Rotator cuff arthropathy (high-riding humeral head, acromiohumeral distance <7 mm)
Proximal humerus fracture (greater/lesser tuberosity, surgical neck)

technique.Grashey View: Patient rotated 35–45° toward affected side; CR perpendicular to glenohumeral joint

procedures.positioning: Grashey: Rotates glenoid cavity into true profile with no humeral head overlap. Scapular Y: Patient anterior oblique 45–60°, CR tangential to scapula blade; humeral head should sit dead center at intersection of Y arms (acromion and coracoid).
procedures.notes: Always perform an axillary or Y view in acute trauma: an AP view alone CANNOT reliably exclude posterior shoulder dislocation.

indications: Fall on outstretched hand (FOOSH) with anatomical snuffbox tenderness

Scapholunate ligament dissociation (Terry Thomas sign: gap >3 mm)
Lunate / Perilunate dislocation and carpal instability (DISI / VISI)

technique.Projections: PA, Lateral, PA with 20° Ulnar Deviation, Scaphoid Oblique 45°

procedures.positioning: PA with ulnar deviation: Wrist flat on IR, gently ulnar-deviate hand without moving forearm; central ray angled 10–15° proximally along long axis of scaphoid to elongate it in profile.
procedures.notes: If snuffbox tenderness is present with normal initial x-rays, immobilize in thumb spica splint and repeat x-rays in 10–14 days, or obtain urgent MRI.

LowerLimb.title: Lower Extremity MSK & Angiography Reference
LowerLimb.content:
Comprehensive lower limb orthopedic and vascular imaging: Pelvis/Acetabulum, Hip joint, Knee meniscal/ligamentous protocols, Ankle Mortise views, and lower extremity run-off CTA/MRA for peripheral artery disease (PAD).

Lower Extremity Run-Off CTA Protocol

Scanned from upper abdominal aorta through the plantar arches of the feet. Requires dynamic pitch matching table velocity to the contrast bolus arrival speed (bolus chase), tracking through common iliac, external iliac, femoral, popliteal, anterior tibial, posterior tibial, and peroneal arteries.

procedures.name: CTA Lower Extremity Run-Off (Aortoiliac to Pedal)
indications: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) with critical limb ischemia or rest pain
Acute lower extremity arterial thrombosis / embolism (the 6 P's)
Popliteal artery aneurysm (bilateral in 50%) and entrapment syndrome
Pre-procedural planning for percutaneous balloon angioplasty, stenting, or bypass
procedures.contrast: 120–140 mL iodinated contrast (350 mg I/mL) @ 4.0–4.5 mL/s + 50 mL saline flush

technique.Coverage: Diaphragm to toes (120–140 cm scan length)
technique.Bolus Tracking: ROI on infrarenal abdominal aorta, trigger 120 HU
technique.Table Speed: Variable pitch / chase mode matching contrast wave (approx 25–30 mm/s)
technique.Reconstructions: 0.625 mm raw, coronal/sagittal MIP run-off displays, curved planar reformations (CPR) of SFA, popliteal, and tibials

procedures.positioning: Patient supine, feet-first. Feet taped together with slight internal rotation to separate tibial and fibular shafts. Elevate legs slightly with foam pad.
procedures.notes: Assess runoff vessels at the ankle: at least one patent direct-to-foot vessel (anterior tibial/dorsalis pedis or posterior tibial) is critical for limb salvage.

procedures.name: CT Knee & Tibial Plateau (Schatzker Fracture Analysis)
indications: High-energy tibial plateau fractures (Schatzker Types I–VI)
Quantification of articular depression (>2–3 mm mandates surgical elevation)
Patellar fracture displacement and extensor mechanism disruption
Post-operative articular alignment and intra-articular loose bodies

technique.Reconstruction: Bone algorithm: WW: 2500, WL: 450 HU; Soft algorithm for periarticular lipohemarthrosis: WW: 400, WL: 40 HU
technique.3D VR: Color-coded 3D volume rendering with femoral subtraction

procedures.positioning: Patient supine, knee in neutral extension, centered in scanner gantry.
procedures.notes: Lipohemarthrosis (fat-blood fluid level in suprapatellar bursa) is pathognomonic for intra-articular fracture communicating with fatty bone marrow.

procedures.name: Pelvis & Hip Radiography (AP Pelvis & Frog-Leg Lateral)
indications: Femoral neck fracture (intracapsular: subcapital, transcervical; Garden classification)
Osteoarthritis of hip (joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, osteophytes, cysts)
Femoroacetabular impingement (FAI: Cam deformity alpha angle, Pincer crossover sign)
Developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) and avascular necrosis (Ficat stages)
procedures.positioning: AP Pelvis: Supine, lower limbs internally rotated 15–20° from hips (places femoral necks parallel to IR and eliminates foreshortening). Frog-leg (Modified Cleaves): Knee flexed ~90°, hip abducted 40–45° laterally.
procedures.notes: Check Shenton's line: smooth continuous curved line formed by inferior border of superior pubic ramus and inferomedial border of femoral neck. Discontinuity indicates fracture or dislocation.

procedures.name: Knee Radiography (AP, Lateral Weight-Bearing, Sunrise View)
indications: Acute knee trauma (Ottawa Knee Rules: age >=55, isolated patellar tenderness, fibular head tenderness, inability to flex 90°, inability to bear weight)
Patellar subluxation / lateral tilt (Merchant / Sunrise axial view)
Tibial spine avulsion fracture (ACL insertion avulsion)
Segond fracture (lateral tibial plateau avulsion, 90% associated with ACL rupture)

technique.Grid: Non-grid for extremities <= 10 cm, or grid for dense knees
technique.Projections: AP Weight-Bearing, True Lateral 20–30° flexion, Merchant/Sunrise 45° axial patellar view

procedures.positioning: AP: Patient standing erect with equal weight distribution. Lateral: Patient lateral recumbent, knee flexed 20–30° (tightens patellar tendon and exposes suprapatellar fat pads without effacing joint fluid). Sunrise: Knee flexed 40–45°, CR angled 30° caudad to horizontal.
procedures.notes: True lateral view allows detection of fat pad displacement and joint effusion measuring >= 5 mm.

procedures.name: Ankle Radiography (AP, Mortise 15° Internal, Lateral)
indications: Ankle inversion / eversion sprain (Ottawa Ankle Rules)
Malleolar fractures (Danis-Weber Type A, B, C; Lauge-Hansen classification)
Syndesmotic diastasis (tibiofibular clear space >6 mm on mortise)
Maisonneuve fracture (high fibular neck fracture associated with medial malleolus disruption)
procedures.positioning: Mortise View: Leg and foot internally rotated 15–20° until intermalleolar line is parallel to IR. This rotates the lateral malleolus out of superimposition with tibia, opening the entire uniform 3–4 mm mortise joint space around talus.
procedures.notes: Always palpate the proximal fibular head in severe ankle injuries to rule out a high Maisonneuve fracture!
